title: Critical WordPress Core Flaw Lets Unauthenticated Attackers Execute Remote Code
content_md: WordPress has released version 7.1.2 to address a critical core vulnerability that could allow unauthenticated attackers to achieve remote code execution under specific server and theme configurations. Tracked as CVE-2026-87902 and GHSA-7hp8-65ch-5whp, the flaw carries a CVSS v4 score of 9.2 and affects WordPress installations dating back to version 4.7. The issue resides in WordPress page-template resolution, specifically within the get_page_template() functionality. An attacker does not need a WordPress account or any privileges to exploit the flaw. Critical WordPress Core Flaw By manipulating page-template handling, they may be able to cause WordPress to include a readable local PHP file located outside the active theme directory. If the included file can be influenced or already exists in a suitable location, the condition can escalate from a path traversal-style issue to remote code execution. Successful exploitation could enable attackers to run arbitrary PHP code in the context of the affected web server, potentially leading to website takeover, data theft, persistent backdoors, malware deployment, or further movement across a hosting environment. The vulnerability was responsibly disclosed by security researcher Robert Ressl. WordPress categorized the flaw as critical because it is remotely reachable and requires no authentication or user interaction. The advisory maps the issue to CWE-98, covering improper control of filenames used in PHP include or require operation
